incidents.vector: Social-engineered abuse of Microsoft Self-Service Password Reset to bypass MFA, then privileged Azure RBAC roles used to invoke management-plane APIs against App Services, Key Vaults, Storage and SQL.
incidents.impact: Identity compromise of IT staff and senior leadership expanded into a cloud-wide breach across Microsoft 365 and Azure; thousands of OneDrive/SharePoint files exfiltrated and production Azure resources accessed, with VPN and remote-access documents specifically targeted.

incidents.vector: A leaked GitHub access token was used by the attacker to authenticate to the Grafana Labs GitHub environment and download the company's codebase.
incidents.impact: Codebase exfiltrated; Grafana publicly refused to pay the ransom, citing FBI guidance. No customer data or production-system access reported. The extortion crew has tried to shake down 100+ companies since September.

incidents.victim: Dozens of enterprises in North America, Australia and the UK
incidents.vector: Voice phishing of employees on personal phones posing as IT help desk, driving victims to lookalike SSO portals; live adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) captures of credentials and MFA codes, followed by registration of an attacker-controlled MFA device.
incidents.impact: Programmatic exfiltration of SharePoint and OneDrive at scale (over a million files in one engagement), branded extortion demands starting in the millions, and aggressive escalation including spam floods, threatening voicemails to executives and swatting against staff.

incidents.victim: US gas stations (automatic tank gauge systems)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of internet-exposed automatic tank gauge (ATG) systems with no password protection, allowing changes to display readings.
incidents.impact: Attackers altered tank display readings but not actual fuel levels; no operational disruption reported. CNN-reported intrusion fits a broader pattern of Iran-affiliated targeting of US OT during the ongoing US/Israel–Iran conflict.

incidents.vector: A CISA contractor (Nightwing) maintained a public 'Private-CISA' GitHub repository with admin AWS GovCloud tokens, plaintext credentials for internal CISA systems, and internal build/deploy files; the contractor had explicitly disabled GitHub's default secret-scanning protection.
incidents.impact: Three AWS GovCloud accounts and dozens of internal CISA systems (including the DevSecOps Landing Zone and code artifactory) were exposed; researchers confirmed credentials were live, and AWS keys inexplicably remained valid 48 hours after disclosure. CISA says no evidence of compromise but is investigating.

incidents.vector: CVE-2026-42897, a cross-site scripting flaw in Outlook Web Access; a specially crafted email triggers attacker JavaScript when opened in OWA, yielding mailbox compromise and session-token theft.
incidents.impact: Active exploitation confirmed and added to CISA's KEV catalog, but no patch is available — Microsoft is shipping only an emergency mitigation. Attackers can read, send and modify mail, steal session tokens, and plant persistent forwarding rules, opening the door to BEC and ransomware.

incidents.vector: CVE-2026-20182, an authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager, allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain administrative privileges. Separate threat clusters are also exploiting earlier disclosed SD-WAN bugs (CVE-2026-20133/20128/20122) using public PoC and JSP webshells.
incidents.impact: Talos confirms ongoing exploitation since March 2026, with attacker infrastructure overlapping operational relay box (ORB) networks. Customers urged to apply the February 2026 software updates and Cisco's May 2026 advisory.

incidents.vector: The financially motivated actor behind the Shai-Hulud self-replicating worm released its source code on GitHub on May 12; copycats immediately published typosquatted NPM packages that pair an infostealer with code that republishes poisoned dependencies from compromised maintainer accounts.
incidents.impact: Four malicious clone packages with their own command-and-control are already live on NPM (~2,600 combined weekly downloads, plus a DDoS botnet payload). Defenders warn the release creates a 'population' of worm variants with distinct C2 and signing keys — much harder to defend against than the original.

incidents.victim: Instructure (Canvas LMS) — ~9,000 schools, universities and businesses
incidents.vector: Compromised 'Free-For-Teacher' Canvas accounts with excessive standing privileges were used for lateral movement and mass exfiltration; a second breach defaced login pages with a ransom note after Instructure publicly claimed the incident was contained.
incidents.impact: 3.65 TB of data covering ~275 million students and faculty exfiltrated, including names, emails, student IDs and messages. Canvas was pulled offline mid-finals; Congress opened a formal investigation and called the Instructure CEO to testify. Attackers claim digital confirmation of data destruction, but accountability for affected institutions remains open.

incidents.vector: CVE-2026-6973, an improper input validation flaw in Ivanti EPMM, under active exploitation.
incidents.impact: CISA added the bug to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog with mandatory federal remediation. Yet another actively exploited zero-day in Ivanti's mobile-device management product line.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall customers
incidents.vector: CVE-2026-0300, a buffer overflow in the PAN-OS User-ID Authentication Portal ('Captive Portal') service, allows unauthenticated remote code execution as root on internet-exposed firewalls. Attackers injected shellcode into the nginx worker.
incidents.impact: Limited but disciplined exploitation since April 9: attackers cleared logs, deployed EarthWorm and ReverseSocks5 tunneling tools, enumerated Active Directory using firewall service-account credentials, and used a SAML flood to fail-over and compromise a second appliance.

incidents.victim: DAEMON Tools (AVB Disc Soft) and selected downstream users in Russia, Belarus and Thailand
incidents.vector: DAEMON Tools installers — signed with the vendor's legitimate certificate — were trojanized since at least April 8. The first-stage backdoor profiled hosts (MAC, hostname, locale, DNS, processes) and selectively deployed the QUIC RAT second stage on a small set of high-value victims.
incidents.impact: Several thousand infections globally, but the QUIC RAT was deployed on only about a dozen targets in government, scientific, manufacturing and retail organisations. Tradecraft mirrors prior Chinese APT supply-chain operations against Notepad++ and CCleaner.

incidents.victim: Government entities in South America and southeastern Europe
incidents.vector: Custom malware including a C#-based variant of the FinalDraft/SquidDoor backdoor ('NetDraft'), an updated CloudSorcerer backdoor (also seen against Russian government targets in 2024), the VSHELL backdoor with its SNOWLIGHT stager, and a new Rust-based stager ('SNOWRUST'); combined with Impacket and other open-source tooling for credential extraction and lateral movement.
incidents.impact: Long-term, low-tempo espionage access maintained against government bodies in South America since at least late 2024 and in southeastern Europe through 2025. Strong overlap with the China-nexus Jewelbug/REF7707 activity cluster.
